In preeclampsia this remodeling is shallow and incomplete, so the placenta becomes ischemic and releases antiangiogenic factors, mainly soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase 1 (sFlt-1) and soluble endoglin, which bind VEGF, PlGF, and TGF-beta and cause widespread maternal endothelial dysfunction: hypertension, proteinuria (glomerular endotheliosis), thrombocytopenia, liver injury, and cerebral symptoms. A systolic pressure of 160 mm Hg or higher or a diastolic pressure of 110 mm Hg or higher, new cerebral or visual symptoms, a platelet count below 100,000/mm3, and doubled aminotransferases all qualify as severe features. Antiphospholipid antibodies increase the risk of preeclampsia but are not its usual mechanism. Human placental lactogen causes maternal insulin resistance and contributes to gestational diabetes. A complete hydatidiform mole (paternal-only genome) can cause preeclampsia before 20 weeks, with very high hCG. Severe ADAMTS13 deficiency causes thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, with schistocytes and microangiopathic hemolysis.
explicacao_pt: Na pré-eclâmpsia, o citotrofoblasto não remodela as artérias espiraladas maternas, que continuam estreitas e de alta resistência. A placenta isquêmica libera fatores antiangiogênicos, como sFlt-1 e endoglina solúvel, que causam disfunção endotelial sistêmica: hipertensão, proteinúria, plaquetopenia, lesão hepática e sintomas neurológicos. Pressão sistólica de 160 mm Hg ou mais ou diastólica de 110 mm Hg ou mais, sintomas visuais, plaquetas abaixo de 100.000/mm3 e transaminases acima do dobro do normal são critérios de gravidade.
fonte: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. Practice Bulletin No. 222: Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia. Obstet Gynecol 2020;135:e237-60; Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th ed.

vinheta: A 29-year-old man and his wife come to the physician because they have been unable to conceive for 2 years. He has had chronic sinusitis and recurrent bronchitis since childhood and has a productive cough on most days. Examination shows crackles at both lung bases. The apical impulse is palpable in the right fifth intercostal space at the midclavicular line. The testes are normal in size, and the vas deferens is palpable bilaterally. Semen analysis shows normal volume and sperm concentration; sperm motility is 0%, and a vital stain shows that most sperm are alive. CT of the chest shows bronchiectasis of both lower lobes and situs inversus.
pergunta: A defect in which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's infertility?

alternativas.texto: Axonemal dynein arms
Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator
Lysosomal enzyme targeting by mannose 6-phosphate
Sertoli cell androgen-binding protein
Tight junctions between Sertoli cells

explicacao: Correct: axonemal dynein arms. Motile cilia and the sperm flagellum share a 9+2 axoneme in which dynein arms, ATPase motors attached to the outer doublet microtubules, make the doublets slide against each other to produce bending. In primary ciliary dyskinesia (mutations in genes such as DNAH5 and DNAI1), absent or defective dynein arms leave cilia and flagella immotile. Failed mucociliary clearance causes chronic sinusitis, otitis, and bronchiectasis; immotile but viable sperm cause male infertility; and loss of the motile cilia of the embryonic node randomizes left-right asymmetry, so about half of patients have situs inversus (Kartagener syndrome). CFTR mutations cause congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens with obstructive azoospermia, so sperm would be absent and the vas not palpable. Defective mannose 6-phosphate tagging causes I-cell disease, a severe lysosomal disorder of infancy. Androgen-binding protein deficiency would impair spermatogenesis and lower sperm count. Disrupted Sertoli tight junctions (blood-testis barrier) expose germ cells to the immune system and impair spermatogenesis rather than motility alone.
explicacao_pt: Na discinesia ciliar primária, defeitos nos braços de dineína do axonema impedem o batimento de cílios e flagelos, que têm o mesmo arranjo 9+2 de microtúbulos. O resultado é sinusite e bronquiectasias por falha da depuração mucociliar e espermatozoides vivos, mas imóveis. Cerca de metade dos pacientes tem situs inversus, porque os cílios do nó embrionário definem a lateralidade (síndrome de Kartagener).
fonte: Pawlina W. Ross Histology: A Text and Atlas, 8th ed. (Cilia and the axoneme); Lucas JS et al. European Respiratory Society guidelines for the diagnosis of primary ciliary dyskinesia. Eur Respir J 2017;49:1601090.

vinheta: A 49-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by police after he was found wandering and confused. He has a long history of alcohol use disorder. Temperature is 36.6°C (97.9°F), pulse is 104/min, and blood pressure is 112/70 mm Hg. He is thin and disheveled and is disoriented to place and time. Examination shows bilateral horizontal nystagmus, weakness of lateral gaze in both eyes, and a wide-based, unsteady gait. Serum glucose concentration is 78 mg/dL.
pergunta: Measurement of which of the following enzyme activities in this patient's erythrocytes is most likely to show a decrease?

alternativas.texto: Aminolevulinate dehydratase
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase
Glutathione reductase
Pyruvate kinase
Transketolase

explicacao: Correct: transketolase. Confusion, ophthalmoplegia, and ataxia in a malnourished patient with alcohol use disorder indicate Wernicke encephalopathy from thiamine deficiency. Thiamine pyrophosphate is the cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase, and transketolase. Transketolase, in the nonoxidative pentose phosphate pathway, is active in erythrocytes, so low erythrocyte transketolase activity that rises when thiamine pyrophosphate is added in vitro confirms deficiency. Thiamine should be given before or with glucose, because glucose metabolism consumes the remaining cofactor. Aminolevulinate dehydratase is inhibited by lead. Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase and pyruvate kinase deficiencies are inherited causes of hemolysis, not vitamin deficiencies. Erythrocyte glutathione reductase depends on FAD and is used to assess riboflavin status.
explicacao_pt: A encefalopatia de Wernicke (confusão, oftalmoparesia e ataxia) resulta de deficiência de tiamina, cuja forma ativa, o pirofosfato de tiamina, é cofator da piruvato desidrogenase, da alfa-cetoglutarato desidrogenase e da transcetolase. A transcetolase da via das pentoses está presente nas hemácias, e sua atividade baixa confirma a deficiência. A tiamina deve ser dada antes da glicose ou junto com ela.
fonte: Ferrier DR. Lippincott Illustrated Reviews: Biochemistry, 8th ed. (Vitamins); Sechi G, Serra A. Wernicke's encephalopathy: new clinical settings and recent advances in diagnosis and management. Lancet Neurol 2007;6:442-55.

vinheta: A 19-year-old woman is brought to the physician 2 weeks after an episode of severe headache, vomiting, and loss of vision in the left visual field that has partially resolved. She has short stature and has had exercise intolerance since childhood. MRI of the brain shows cortical lesions in the right occipital lobe that do not correspond to a single arterial territory. Serum lactate concentration is increased. A muscle biopsy specimen shows ragged red fibers with modified Gomori trichrome stain. Her mother has diabetes mellitus and sensorineural hearing loss, her maternal uncle had seizures and died at the age of 30 years, and her brother is asymptomatic. Her father and his relatives are healthy. Genetic testing of the patient identifies the m.3243A>G variant in the mitochondrial MT-TL1 gene.
pergunta: Which of the following best explains the variable severity of disease among this patient's maternal relatives?

alternativas.texto: Anticipation from trinucleotide repeat expansion
Genomic imprinting
Germline mosaicism
Heteroplasmy
Locus heterogeneity
Uniparental disomy

explicacao: Correct: heteroplasmy. MELAS (mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes) is most often caused by m.3243A>G in the mitochondrial tRNA-Leu gene. Mitochondrial DNA is inherited only from the mother. Each cell contains hundreds to thousands of mtDNA copies, and a mixture of mutant and normal genomes (heteroplasmy) is distributed unevenly among oocytes (the mitochondrial bottleneck) and among tissues. Disease appears in a tissue when the mutant fraction exceeds a threshold, so relatives with the same variant range from asymptomatic to diabetes and deafness to severe encephalomyopathy. Anticipation (earlier onset and greater severity in successive generations) is typical of trinucleotide repeat disorders such as Huntington disease and myotonic dystrophy; here severity varies within one generation. Genomic imprinting produces parent-of-origin effects in nuclear genes (Prader-Willi and Angelman syndromes). Germline mosaicism explains several affected children born to unaffected parents. Locus heterogeneity means mutations in different genes cause the same phenotype, whereas this family shares a single variant. Uniparental disomy is inheritance of both copies of a chromosome from one parent.
explicacao_pt: Na MELAS, a variante patogênica está no DNA mitocondrial, herdado só da mãe. Cada célula carrega centenas a milhares de cópias de mtDNA, e a proporção de cópias mutadas (heteroplasmia) varia entre pessoas e entre tecidos; a doença aparece quando essa proporção passa de um limiar. Por isso, parentes pela linha materna com a mesma variante podem ter desde quadro leve, como diabetes e surdez, até encefalopatia grave.
fonte: Nussbaum RL, McInnes RR, Willard HF. Thompson & Thompson Genetics in Medicine, 9th ed.; Gorman GS et al. Mitochondrial diseases. Nat Rev Dis Primers 2016;2:16080.

vinheta: A 22-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department because of fever, vomiting, watery diarrhea, and lightheadedness for 1 day. She is menstruating and has been using tampons. Temperature is 39.9°C (103.8°F), pulse is 128/min, and blood pressure is 78/42 mm Hg. Examination shows diffuse macular erythroderma, including the palms, and nonpurulent conjunctival injection. Pelvic examination shows a tampon in the vaginal vault, which she says was inserted about 36 hours earlier. Laboratory studies show a platelet count of 88,000/mm3, serum creatinine concentration of 2.1 mg/dL, creatine kinase activity of 1,800 U/L, and AST activity of 112 U/L. Blood cultures show no growth at 48 hours. Culture of a vaginal swab grows coagulase-positive, gram-positive cocci in clusters.
pergunta: The toxin responsible for this patient's condition acts by which of the following mechanisms?

alternativas.texto: Activation of complement by lipooligosaccharide shed in outer membrane blebs
Binding of MHC class II and T-cell receptor Vβ regions outside the peptide groove
Cleavage of desmoglein 1 in the granular layer of the epidermis
Inhibition of protein synthesis by ADP-ribosylation of elongation factor 2
Pore formation in host cell membranes by oligomerized toxin monomers

explicacao: Correct: binding of MHC class II and T-cell receptor Vβ regions outside the peptide groove. Toxic shock syndrome toxin-1 of Staphylococcus aureus is a superantigen. It links MHC class II molecules on antigen-presenting cells to the variable region of the T-cell receptor beta chain without antigen processing, so it activates a large fraction of T cells regardless of their antigen specificity. The resulting surge of IL-2, IFN-gamma, TNF-alpha, and IL-1 causes fever, diffuse erythroderma with later desquamation, capillary leak, shock, and multiorgan injury. Blood cultures are usually negative because the toxin is absorbed from a local focus, such as a retained tampon, which must be removed. Complement activation by lipooligosaccharide explains meningococcemia. Desmoglein 1 cleavage by exfoliative toxins causes staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome, usually in young children, without shock. ADP-ribosylation of elongation factor 2 is the mechanism of diphtheria toxin and Pseudomonas exotoxin A. Pore formation describes staphylococcal alpha-toxin and streptolysin O.
explicacao_pt: A toxina 1 da síndrome do choque tóxico (TSST-1) do Staphylococcus aureus é um superantígeno: liga o MHC de classe II à região Vβ do receptor do linfócito T fora do sulco de apresentação de peptídeos. Isso ativa grande número de linfócitos T de forma policlonal, com liberação maciça de IL-2, interferon gama e TNF, o que causa febre, eritrodermia, choque e falência de órgãos. As hemoculturas costumam ser negativas, e retirar o foco (o tampão) faz parte do tratamento.
fonte: Murphy K, Weaver C. Janeway's Immunobiology, 10th ed. (Superantigens); Ryan KJ. Sherris & Ryan's Medical Microbiology, 8th ed.; CDC. Toxic Shock Syndrome (Other Than Streptococcal) 2011 Case Definition.

vinheta: A 61-year-old man in the intensive care unit has received a continuous intravenous infusion of sodium nitroprusside for 3 days for a hypertensive emergency. Today he has become confused and agitated. Temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F), pulse is 118/min, respirations are 28/min, and blood pressure is 128/76 mm Hg. Pulse oximetry shows an oxygen saturation of 99% on 2 L/min of oxygen by nasal cannula. Arterial blood gas analysis shows: pH 7.24; PaCO2 26 mm Hg; PaO2 98 mm Hg; HCO3- 11 mEq/L. Serum lactate concentration is 9.2 mmol/L. Central venous oxygen saturation is 90%. Methemoglobin and carboxyhemoglobin fractions are each 1%.
pergunta: Which of the following best explains this patient's metabolic abnormalities?

alternativas.texto: Binding of carbon monoxide to hemoglobin
Inhibition of cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV)
Inhibition of mitochondrial ATP synthase (complex V)
Oxidation of hemoglobin iron to the ferric state
Uncoupling of the proton gradient from ATP synthesis

explicacao: Correct: inhibition of cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV). Each nitroprusside molecule contains five cyanide groups. Cyanide is normally converted by rhodanese, using thiosulfate as sulfur donor, to thiocyanate, which the kidneys excrete. With prolonged or high-dose infusions, thiosulfate stores are exhausted and cyanide binds the ferric iron of cytochrome a3 in complex IV, halting oxidative phosphorylation. Cells cannot use oxygen, so venous blood stays highly saturated (a narrow arteriovenous oxygen difference), and anaerobic glycolysis produces a lactic acidosis with an increased anion gap. Treatment is to stop the infusion and give hydroxocobalamin or sodium thiosulfate. Carbon monoxide poisoning would raise the carboxyhemoglobin fraction, and methemoglobinemia (ferric heme) would raise the methemoglobin fraction; both are normal. Inhibition of ATP synthase (oligomycin) is an experimental mechanism that also slows electron transport but is not caused by nitroprusside. Uncouplers (2,4-dinitrophenol, high-dose salicylates) increase oxygen consumption and heat production, so venous saturation falls and hyperthermia develops.
explicacao_pt: Cada molécula de nitroprussiato contém cinco grupos cianeto, que a rodanase converte em tiocianato usando tiossulfato. Em infusões prolongadas ou com dose alta, o cianeto se acumula, liga-se ao ferro férrico da citocromo c oxidase (complexo IV) e as células deixam de usar o oxigênio. O sangue venoso continua muito oxigenado e surge acidose lática; o tratamento é suspender a infusão e dar hidroxocobalamina ou tiossulfato de sódio.
fonte: Brunton LL et al. Goodman & Gilman's The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 14th ed.; Nelson LS et al. Goldfrank's Toxicologic Emergencies, 11th ed. (Cyanide and hydrogen sulfide).

vinheta: A new rapid assay for a bacterial infection is evaluated in 1,000 adults who come to an urgent care clinic with symptoms. All participants also undergo the reference-standard test. Of the 200 participants with infection by the reference standard, 180 have a positive result on the new assay. Of the 800 participants without infection by the reference standard, 720 have a negative result on the new assay.
pergunta: Which of the following is closest to the negative predictive value of the new assay in this population?
explicacao: Correct: 97%. Build the 2 x 2 table: true positives 180, false negatives 20 (200 - 180), true negatives 720, false positives 80 (800 - 720). Negative predictive value = TN / (TN + FN) = 720 / (720 + 20) = 720/740, about 97%. 10% is the false-positive rate (80/800), which equals 1 - specificity. 69% is the positive predictive value, TP / (TP + FP) = 180/260. 80% is the proportion of participants without infection (1 - prevalence of 20%). 90% is both the sensitivity (180/200) and the specificity (720/800). Unlike sensitivity and specificity, predictive values depend on prevalence: at a lower prevalence, NPV would rise further and PPV would fall.
explicacao_pt: O valor preditivo negativo é a proporção de verdadeiros negativos entre todos os resultados negativos: 720 dividido por 740 (720 verdadeiros negativos e 20 falsos negativos), cerca de 97%. A sensibilidade e a especificidade são de 90%, e o valor preditivo positivo é de 180/260, cerca de 69%. Os valores preditivos variam com a prevalência, enquanto sensibilidade e especificidade não variam.
fonte: Celentano DD, Szklo M. Gordis Epidemiology, 6th ed. (Assessing the validity and reliability of diagnostic and screening tests).

vinheta: Investigators evaluate a new imaging test to screen asymptomatic adults for pancreatic cancer. Among patients whose cancer was detected by screening, median survival measured from the date of diagnosis is 3.1 years, compared with 1.2 years among unscreened patients whose cancer was diagnosed after symptoms appeared. Tumors detected by screening and those detected clinically have similar histologic grade and growth rates. The mean age at death from pancreatic cancer and the pancreatic cancer mortality rate per 100,000 person-years do not differ between the screened and unscreened cohorts.
pergunta: Which of the following best explains the apparent survival benefit associated with screening?

alternativas.texto: Attrition bias
Lead-time bias
Length-time bias
Observer bias
Recall bias
Selection bias

explicacao: Correct: lead-time bias. Screening moves the date of diagnosis earlier in the natural history of the disease. If treatment does not change the course, the time of death is the same, but survival measured from diagnosis looks longer simply because the clock starts sooner. The unchanged age at death and unchanged disease-specific mortality show that screening produced no real benefit. Trials of screening should therefore use disease-specific mortality, not survival from diagnosis, as the outcome. Attrition bias arises from differential loss to follow-up. Length-time bias occurs when screening preferentially detects slow-growing, less aggressive tumors, which is excluded here because grade and growth rates are similar. Observer bias arises when knowledge of exposure influences outcome assessment. Recall bias affects self-reported past exposures, typically in case-control studies. Selection bias (for example, healthier volunteers choosing to be screened) would usually also change mortality in the screened group.
explicacao_pt: O viés de tempo de antecipação (lead-time bias) ocorre quando o rastreamento adianta o diagnóstico sem adiar a morte; a sobrevida contada a partir do diagnóstico aumenta só porque o relógio começa antes. A idade de morte e a mortalidade por câncer iguais nos dois grupos mostram que não houve benefício real. Por isso, ensaios de rastreamento devem usar a mortalidade específica, e não a sobrevida desde o diagnóstico, como desfecho.
fonte: Celentano DD, Szklo M. Gordis Epidemiology, 6th ed. (Epidemiologic approach to evaluating screening programs).

vinheta: A 74-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus is hospitalized for wet gangrene of the right forefoot. The vascular surgeon recommends a below-the-knee amputation and explains that without surgery the infection may spread and could be fatal, and that antibiotics alone are less likely to control it. The patient declines surgery. He accurately restates the risks, says that he understands he could die, and explains that losing his leg would end his work as a farmer, which he values more than a longer life. He gives the same explanation on 2 consecutive days. He is alert and oriented, scores 29 of 30 on the Mini-Mental State Examination, and shows no signs of depression or psychosis. His daughter insists that the surgery be performed. Temperature is 37.8°C (100.0°F), and blood pressure is 128/76 mm Hg.
pergunta: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

alternativas.texto: Ask the daughter to provide consent as surrogate decision-maker
Obtain a court order authorizing the amputation
Perform the amputation under the emergency exception
Request a psychiatric evaluation to declare him incompetent
Respect the refusal and continue antibiotics and wound care

explicacao: Correct: respect the refusal and continue antibiotics and wound care. Decision-making capacity requires that the patient understand the relevant information, appreciate how it applies to his own situation, reason about the options, and communicate a stable choice. The treating physician can assess capacity, which is specific to each decision. This patient meets every element, and his choice reflects his stated values, so he may refuse even life-saving treatment; the physician should continue the best alternative care and keep surgery available if he changes his mind. A surrogate decides only when the patient lacks capacity, and family disagreement does not override a capable patient. A court order is not needed when a capable patient refuses. The emergency exception applies only when the patient cannot consent and delay would cause serious harm. Psychiatric consultation can help when capacity is uncertain, but it is not a tool to override a capable refusal, and 'competence' is a legal determination made by a court.
explicacao_pt: Paciente com capacidade de decisão pode recusar tratamento, mesmo que a recusa traga risco de morte. Ele compreende as informações, reconhece a própria situação, raciocina com coerência e mantém a escolha, e quem avalia a capacidade é o médico assistente. A família só decide quando o paciente não tem capacidade; a conduta é respeitar a recusa, oferecer o melhor tratamento alternativo e manter a cirurgia como opção.
fonte: Appelbaum PS. Assessment of patients' competence to consent to treatment. N Engl J Med 2007;357:1834-40; American Medical Association. Code of Medical Ethics, Opinion 2.1.1 (Informed Consent).

vinheta: A 58-year-old woman is hospitalized for community-acquired pneumonia. Enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously once daily was ordered for prophylaxis of venous thromboembolism, but because of a transcription error she received a 60-mg dose this morning. A second-year resident discovers the error 3 hours later. The patient has no bleeding, her hemoglobin concentration and platelet count are unchanged from yesterday, and her vital signs are within normal limits. The resident is concerned that telling the patient will damage her trust in the team.
pergunta: Which of the following is the most appropriate action by the resident?

alternativas.texto: Disclose the error to the patient and file a safety event report
Document the dose in the chart without informing the patient
File a safety event report and inform the patient only if bleeding occurs
Inform the patient after the risk management office reviews the event
Report the pharmacist involved to the state board of pharmacy

explicacao: Correct: disclose the error to the patient and file a safety event report. Errors that reach the patient should be disclosed promptly and honestly, even when no harm is evident: the physician explains what happened, apologizes, describes the monitoring plan (here, observation for bleeding), and explains what will be done to prevent recurrence. Reporting through the institutional safety system allows a systems-focused (root cause) analysis of the transcription process. Charting the dose without telling the patient conceals the error. Waiting until bleeding occurs, or until risk management finishes its review, delays disclosure the patient is owed. Reporting an individual to a licensing board is a punitive first step that ignores the system failure and is not the resident's immediate obligation.
explicacao_pt: Erros que chegam ao paciente devem ser comunicados a ele com clareza, mesmo sem dano aparente, com explicação do ocorrido, pedido de desculpas e plano de vigilância. A notificação ao sistema institucional de segurança permite analisar a causa raiz e corrigir o processo, sem foco em punição individual. Adiar a conversa até haver dano ou até a avaliação do setor de gestão de risco fere o dever de transparência.
fonte: American Medical Association. Code of Medical Ethics, Opinion 8.6 (Promoting Patient Safety); Gallagher TH, Studdert D, Levinson W. Disclosing harmful medical errors to patients. N Engl J Med 2007;356:2713-9.

vinheta: A 46-year-old woman who moved to the United States from Brazil 1 year ago comes to the clinic to discuss the results of a breast biopsy, which shows invasive ductal carcinoma. She speaks Portuguese and very limited English. Her 14-year-old son, who is fluent in both languages, accompanies her and offers to interpret. The clinic has access to professional medical interpreters by telephone and video.
pergunta: Which of the following is the most appropriate way to communicate the biopsy results to this patient?

alternativas.texto: Ask a bilingual receptionist from the clinic to interpret
Ask the son to interpret because he is fluent in both languages
Communicate through a translation application on a mobile phone
Request a professional medical interpreter by telephone or video
Use simple English supported by written materials in English

explicacao: Correct: request a professional medical interpreter by telephone or video. Patients with limited English proficiency have better comprehension and fewer clinically significant errors when a trained medical interpreter is used, and in the United States Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act requires covered entities to offer qualified interpreters and not to rely on minor children to interpret except in an emergency. Using the son also places a child in the role of delivering a cancer diagnosis to his mother and may lead to filtering of information. Untrained bilingual staff make more interpretation errors and raise confidentiality concerns. Machine translation applications are not reliable for complex, high-stakes conversations. Simple English and English-language materials do not overcome the language barrier and would not support informed decisions about treatment.
explicacao_pt: Para pacientes com proficiência limitada em inglês, o padrão nos EUA é usar intérprete médico qualificado, presencial, por telefone ou por vídeo; a Seção 1557 do Affordable Care Act veda o uso de menores como intérpretes, salvo em emergência. O filho adolescente, além do risco de erros de tradução, ficaria no papel de dar à mãe um diagnóstico de câncer. Funcionários bilíngues sem formação e aplicativos de tradução não oferecem a precisão necessária para uma notícia difícil.
fonte: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. Nondiscrimination in Health Programs and Activities (Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act), 45 CFR 92.201; Karliner LS et al. Do professional interpreters improve clinical care for patients with limited English proficiency? A systematic review. Health Serv Res 2007;42:727-54.
